page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.large is a storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The hardware profile is built on the arm64 architecture featuring AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 cores based on the ARMv9 instruction set. It provides 2 dedicated physical cores (2 vCPUs) running at a clock rate of 2.8 GHz, accompanied by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. Storage is anchored by an integrated 1250 GB NVMe SSD, while the baseline network interface throughput operates at 2 Gbps. No dedicated GPUs are present.

Benchmark evaluations highlight the balance between single-thread efficiency and aggregate core throughput. The instance demonstrates average baseline behavior in Geekbench single-core (1810.0) and stress-ng single-core (1706.88), with strong performance in single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.33 GB/sec. Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth achieves 56.68 GB/sec, placing it within the middle tier. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics scale proportionally to its low physical core count, yielding lower comparative results in multi-core stress-ng (3402.07), Geekbench multi-core (3241.0), and Clang software compilation (4381.0). In-memory write performance sits at 22.2 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput reaches 4.61 million operations per second.

Given its high storage-to-compute ratio and generous memory allocation per core, the i8ge.large delivers balanced cost efficiency for IO-bound applications requiring fast local storage rather than extreme CPU parallelization. The primary architectural tradeoff is the small CPU footprint of two vCPUs alongside limited 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, which restricts high-throughput distributed processing or compute-heavy LLM inference. It is primarily suited for local database operations, caching nodes, search engine indices, log aggregation, and lightweight data pipelines needing fast NVMe storage access.
description: Amazon Web Services i8ge.large is a storage-optimized instance powered by a 2-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 (ARMv9 arm64) processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. It is provisioned with 16.0 GB of memory (8.0 GB per core), 1250 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Lacking dedicated GPU hardware, its processing capabilities reflect solid single-thread performance (1810.0 in Geekbench single-core) alongside average database operations and uncached memory reads. Multi-core compute performance is limited by the 2-vCPU configuration, showing lower results in multi-threaded compilation and stress tests. This hardware configuration is most effectively deployed for I/O-intensive workloads, local databases, data buffering, and lightweight caching engines requiring fast NVMe storage paired with dedicated memory per core.
